Intro: I hope you're keeping well. Lately, I've been nostalgic.
I miss walking around the block and basking in the smell of caramelized street sweets. Red, sour hawthorn encased in sugar, bursting on the tongue.
I yearn for the laughter-filled street markets before the stench of violence permeated our senses. Could we ever go back?
I resigned from the Iron Cross, chef. I refuse to exchange one tyranny for another. I will never agree with Svetka.
But I will never agree with that "messiah" either.
We do not win without loving others, chef. It's hard. We're not pawns. We're living things with beating hearts and fragile prides.
We all want. Svetka wants to find a cure to Spoilage, but to do so, she relies on people like you turning them in, and stripping them for parts.
The resistance wants freedom, but can't decide what that means and who gets it. Who gets to live in the sun again—everyone? Even the spoiled?
As for me and you, chef, well, I can't speak for you. But…
I want to walk around the block again someday. I want to turn the corner, and ask a hawker for hawthorn candy, and I want to eat it in the sunshine.
Goodbye, chef. Maybe I'll see you around.
